body.statement:
For design A, \(\mathscr A\) first tests \(m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\).  If this test fails, or if the single bounded-algebraic-sampling call on the raw legal fiber \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) reports emptiness, then \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)=\varnothing\); the input is reported as incompatible and is not rigid under \(|\mathcal T_A(p,m)|=1\).  Otherwise let \(x_0\in\mathcal C_A(T)\) be the returned sample and set \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\).  Then \(|\mathcal T_A(p,m)|=1\) if and only if the single raw-fiber refinement
\[
\mathcal C_A(T)\cap\left\{x:
(\tau_{C,1}(x)-t_{0,1})^2+(\tau_{C,2}(x)-t_{0,2})^2>0
\right\}
\]
is empty.  For design B, emptiness of the single sampling call on \(\mathcal C_B(T)\) is equivalent to \(\mathcal F_B(p)=\varnothing\), and, on a nonempty fiber, the analogous single refinement is empty if and only if \(|\mathcal T_B(p)|=1\).

For an arbitrary real input \(\zeta\), a rigid value is returned as a rational expression in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) only when the compiler constructs such an expression; every other value is returned as a uniquely ordered real element of a finite algebraic extension, encoded by a square-free real-univariate polynomial over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), rational coordinate functions, and Thom sign data.  For rational \(\zeta\), the encoding may be normalized to a square-free integer polynomial and rational isolating data.  Every nonrigid output contains two legal full SCMs with identical observables and identical supplied margins when margins are supplied, but different \(\tau\).  If both raw-fiber witnesses lie in interior support charts, their full-SCM lifts can be chosen strictly positive; no strict-positivity claim is made for a witness on a boundary face.  The exhaustive structural atlas may label the output diagnostically, but neither its enumeration nor a connected-component description is used in the rigidity decision.
body.justification: The theorem proves the necessary-and-sufficient causal classifier using one raw-fiber sample and one unequal-target existential query after the design-A margin check.
body.gap: The former one-sample/all-chart implementation was exact but not minimal because the raw legal fiber is already one semialgebraic set.
body.consumer: Analysts receive incompatibility, one exact causal target, or legal target-changing SCM twins from the two-call engine.
body.proof_tex:
The supplied design-A margin must be validated before the normalized cycle fiber is used.  By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}design\text{-}a\text{-}fiber\text{-}nonempty\text{-}criterion}\),
\[
 \mathcal F_A(p,m)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}
 \ \text{and}\ 
 \mathcal C_A(T)\ne\varnothing .                         \tag{1}
\]
By the design-B part of Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}cycle\text{-}to\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\),
\[
 \mathcal F_B(p)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal C_B(T)\ne\varnothing .                         \tag{2}
\]
Thus failure of the strict-margin test in design A, or emptiness of the applicable raw cycle fiber, is exactly incompatibility.  Its target image is empty, and therefore is not rigid under Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}target\text{-}rigidity}\), which requires cardinality one.

Assume henceforth that the applicable raw fiber is nonempty and denote it by \(X\).  The simplex equalities and inequalities, the nonnegative factorization equations, and, in design B, the shared-\(Z\) polynomial equations and finite disjunction expressing relevance make \(X\) a bounded semialgebraic set over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  The target map
\[
 f(x)=\tau_C(x)
 =\left(\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z}a_{11,2}(z),
          \sum_{z\in\mathcal Z}a_{00,2}(z)\right)        \tag{3}
\]
is polynomial.  Apply Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}one\text{-}sample\text{-}all\text{-}chart\text{-}rigidity}\) to the one-element family \(X_1=X\).  The first bounded-algebraic-sampling call returns \(x_0\in X\); put \(t_0=f(x_0)\).  The only subsequent existential set is
\[
 R(x_0)=X\cap
 \left\{x:
   (f_1(x)-t_{0,1})^2+(f_2(x)-t_{0,2})^2>0
 \right\}.                                                \tag{4}
\]
If \(R(x_0)=\varnothing\), then every \(x\in X\) has \(\|f(x)-t_0\|_2^2=0\), hence \(f(x)=t_0\) and \(f(X)=\{t_0\}\).  Conversely, if \(f(X)=\{t_0\}\), no point satisfies the strict inequality in (4), so \(R(x_0)=\varnothing\).  If (4) is nonempty, the existential-realizability call returns \(x_1\in R(x_0)\), and its defining inequality gives \(f(x_1)\ne f(x_0)\).  This proves the necessary-and-sufficient test with one sampling call and one unequal-target existential call.

Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}cycle\text{-}to\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) is onto and target preserving, so
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal T_A(p,m)
  &=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\},\\
 \mathcal T_B(p)
  &=\{\tau_C(b,a):(b,a,m,g,\pi)\in\mathcal C_B(T)\}.
 \end{aligned}                                             \tag{5}
\]
Consequently, (4) is empty exactly when the applicable causal target set in (5) is a singleton.  If (4) is nonempty, lift \(x_0\) and \(x_1\) separately using that lemma.  The two resulting parameters lie in the same full fiber, hence have identical selected observables and, in design A, the same supplied margin \(m\); target preservation and (4) give different values of \(\tau\).  These are legal target-changing full-SCM twins in the sense of Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}nonrigidity\text{-}certificate}\).  If both cycle witnesses lie in interior support charts, Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}interior\text{-}cycle\text{-}to\text{-}positive\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) makes every response mass, proxy and instrument kernel, treatment probability, and selection probability strictly interior.  That lemma makes no such assertion on a boundary face, which proves the stated qualification.

By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}effective\text{-}semialgebraic\text{-}sampling\text{-}existential}\), the first call represents \(x_0\) by a real-univariate representation with Thom signs over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  The coordinates of \(t_0\) are linear sums of coordinates of \(x_0\), so they belong to the same finite real algebraic extension.  The second call operates over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)\) and, when (4) is nonempty, returns the same kind of exact representation for \(x_1\).  A rational expression over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) is reported only when field arithmetic constructs one.  Otherwise a square-free real-univariate polynomial, rational coordinate functions, and Thom sign data select the ordered real value.  When \(\zeta\) is rational, clearing the guarded observable denominators and applying the square-free-factorization and root-isolation procedures from the same lemma yields a square-free integer polynomial and rational isolating data.  No connected-component description is used.  The optional structural labels mentioned in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}atlas\text{-}handle}\) do not enter (1)--(5) or either mandatory call.  This proves all clauses.
